title: Hydrodynamic fluctuation action and nonequilibrium quasipotential

items.title: Normalized SSEP macroscopic fluctuation action
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and let $\mathbb T^d=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$ carry normalized product Haar measure $dx$, with $dx(\mathbb T^d)=1$. Coordinates and time are dimensionless in the diffusive normalization $D=1$. For $r\in(0,1)$ set the mobility function $\chi(r):=r(1-r)$. For any finite interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$, let $\rho:[a,b]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R$ be a scalar density and let $j:[a,b]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be a vector current. Require both fields to be smooth up to the time endpoints and periodic in space, and require that for some $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$, $\varepsilon\le\rho(t,x)\le1-\varepsilon$ for every $(t,x)$. Call $(\rho,j)$ admissible when it also satisfies the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot j=0$. Define its dimensionless action by

$$\mathcal I_{[a,b]}(\rho,j):=\frac14\int_a^b\int_{\mathbb T^d}\frac{|j(t,x)+\nabla\rho(t,x)|^2}{\rho(t,x)(1-\rho(t,x))}\,dx\,dt.$$

This is the macroscopic fluctuation functional in the stated normalized SSEP coefficient convention. It is a definition of a functional and does not assert a microscopic path-space large-deviation principle or a probability estimate.

items.title: Bernoulli relative free-energy functional
items.statement: For $u\in(0,1)$ define the Bernoulli free-energy density $f(u):=u\log u+(1-u)\log(1-u)$. For a reference density $\bar\rho\in(0,1)$ define $h(u\mid\bar\rho):=f(u)-f(\bar\rho)-\bigl(\log\bar\rho-\log(1-\bar\rho)\bigr)(u-\bar\rho)$. For $d\ge1$, a smooth profile $\rho:\mathbb T^d\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$ with some $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and normalized product Haar measure $dx$ on $\mathbb T^d$, define $\mathcal H_{\bar\rho}(\rho):=\int_{\mathbb T^d}h(\rho(x)\mid\bar\rho)\,dx$. If $\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho\,dx=\bar\rho$, then $\mathcal H_{\bar\rho}(\rho)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(\rho(x))\,dx-f(\bar\rho)$ because the linear term integrates to zero. All logarithm arguments are positive on the stated domains.

items.title: Fixed-mean action quasi-potential
items.statement:
Fix $d\ge1$, $\bar\rho\in(0,1)$, and normalized product Haar measure $dx$ on $\mathbb T^d$. Let $\rho:\mathbb T^d\to(0,1)$ be a smooth target profile whose values are bounded away from $0$ and $1$. A connection of duration $T>0$ from the homogeneous profile $\bar\rho$ to $\rho$ is a smooth pair $(u,j)$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d$, smooth up to the time endpoints and periodic in space, such that for some $\varepsilon_T\in(0,1/2)$ one has $\varepsilon_T\le u(t,x)\le1-\varepsilon_T$, $\int_{\mathbb T^d}u(t,x)\,dx=\bar\rho$ for all $t$, $\partial_tu+\nabla\cdot j=0$, $u(0,x)=\bar\rho$, and $u(T,x)=\rho(x)$. Define

$$\mathcal V_{\bar\rho}(\rho):=\inf\left\{\mathcal I_{[0,T]}(u,j):T>0,\ (u,j)\text{ is a connection of duration }T\text{ from }\bar\rho\text{ to }\rho\right\},$$

with the infimum of the empty set defined to be $+\infty$. The action is the functional defined in the preceding item.

items.title: Equilibrium action time-reversal identity
items.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $T>0$, and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Let $\rho:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$ be a scalar field and $j:[0,T]\times\mathbb T^d\to\mathbb R^d$ a vector field, both smooth up to the time endpoints and periodic in space. Assume $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot j=0$. Set $f(u):=u\log u+(1-u)\log(1-u)$ for $0<u<1$, and define the reversed paths by $\rho^\theta(t,x):=\rho(T-t,x)$ and $j^\theta(t,x):=-j(T-t,x)$. Then

$$\mathcal I_{[0,T]}(\rho,j)-\mathcal I_{[0,T]}(\rho^\theta,j^\theta)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(\rho(T,x))\,dx-\int_{\mathbb T^d}f(\rho(0,x))\,dx.$$

Here $\mathcal I$ is the normalized SSEP action with $\chi(u)=u(1-u)$.

items.title: Small-action bridge to a relaxed equilibrium profile
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge1$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $\bar\rho\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$. Let $\rho:\mathbb T^d\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$ be a smooth real periodic profile with $\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho\,dx=\bar\rho$. Use normalized product Haar measure and the Fourier conventions $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i k\cdot x)$ and $\widehat\rho(k)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho(x)e_{-k}(x)\,dx$. Define $\rho_0=\rho$ and, for $s>0$, define the heat profile

$$\rho_s(x):=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}e^{-4\pi^2|k|^2s}\widehat\rho(k)e_k(x).$$

Then $\rho_s$ is smooth up to $s=0$ on every compact time interval and $\rho_s\to\bar\rho$ in $C^\infty(\mathbb T^d)$ as $s\to\infty$. For every $S\ge1$ there is a smooth connector $(\sigma^S,\kappa^S)$ on $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^d$ from the constant profile $\bar\rho$ to $\rho_S$, with fixed mean $\bar\rho$, values in $[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$, and $\partial_t\sigma^S+\nabla\cdot\kappa^S=0$. At $t=1$, all time and space derivatives of this connector agree with those of the reversed heat segment $(\rho_{S+1-t},+\nabla\rho_{S+1-t})$. Its action satisfies $\mathcal I_{[0,1]}(\sigma^S,\kappa^S)\to0$ as $S\to\infty$.

items.title: Equilibrium SSEP quasi-potential on a torus
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\ge1$, let $\bar\rho\in(0,1)$, and let $\rho:\mathbb T^d\to[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]$ be a smooth real periodic profile for some $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ with $\int_{\mathbb T^d}\rho\,dx=\bar\rho$, where $dx$ is normalized product Haar measure. For the fixed-mean action quasi-potential $\mathcal V_{\bar\rho}$ and Bernoulli relative free-energy functional $\mathcal H_{\bar\rho}$ defined above, one has

$$\mathcal V_{\bar\rho}(\rho)=\mathcal H_{\bar\rho}(\rho)=\int_{\mathbb T^d}\left[\rho(x)\log\frac{\rho(x)}{\bar\rho}+(1-\rho(x))\log\frac{1-\rho(x)}{1-\bar\rho}\right]dx.$$

This is the homogeneous-equilibrium, fixed-mean torus variational result for the defined continuum action.

title: Hydrodynamic fluctuation action and nonequilibrium quasipotential — Examples

items.title: Two-site boundary-driven SSEP has a nonproduct stationary law for unequal reservoir rates
items.statement:
Fix $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1)$ and set $\Omega=\{0,1\}^2$. For $\eta=(\eta_1,\eta_2)\in\Omega$, let $\eta_i$ denote its $i$th coordinate. Time is measured in units of the bond-swap rate, so that this rate is $1$. For every real function $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, define the generator $L$ acting on observables by

$$
(Lg)(\eta):=\alpha(1-\eta_1)\bigl(g(1,\eta_2)-g(\eta)\bigr)+(1-\alpha)\eta_1\bigl(g(0,\eta_2)-g(\eta)\bigr)+\beta(1-\eta_2)\bigl(g(\eta_1,1)-g(\eta)\bigr)+(1-\beta)\eta_2\bigl(g(\eta_1,0)-g(\eta)\bigr)+\mathbf 1_{\{\eta_1\ne\eta_2\}}\bigl(g(\eta_2,\eta_1)-g(\eta)\bigr).
$$

Here $\mathbf 1_A$ is $1$ when the condition $A$ holds and $0$ otherwise. This rate formula specifies the two reservoir flips and the bond swap of the finite-state continuous-time chain. Let $\mathcal P(\Omega)$ be the set of probability mass functions $\pi:\Omega\to[0,1]$, so $\sum_{\eta\in\Omega}\pi(\eta)=1$. A law $\pi\in\mathcal P(\Omega)$ is stationary when $\sum_{\eta\in\Omega}\pi(\eta)(Lg)(\eta)=0$ for every real $g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Define $\mathbb E_\pi[g]:=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega}\pi(\eta)g(\eta)$, $m_i:=\mathbb E_\pi[\eta_i]$, and

$$\operatorname{Cov}_\pi(\eta_1,\eta_2):=\mathbb E_\pi[\eta_1\eta_2]-m_1m_2.$$

For $i=1,2$, the marginal is $\pi_i(a):=\sum_{\eta\in\Omega:\,\eta_i=a}\pi(\eta)$ for $a\in\{0,1\}$; $\pi$ is a product law when $\pi(a,b)=\pi_1(a)\pi_2(b)$ for all $a,b\in\{0,1\}$. The unique stationary law of this chain has

$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi}(\eta_1,\eta_2)=-\frac{(\alpha-\beta)^2}{18}.$$

Consequently, the stationary law is not a product when $\alpha\ne\beta$. This is an exact finite-chain correlation example, not a derivation of the continuum quasi-potential.
